facts.raw_span: 2-year history of progressively worsening fever
weight loss, night sweats, and a dry cough
chronic lower back pain without neurologic deficits
painful nonhealing ulcer on his right hallux
two sputum GeneXpert tests at local clinics, both negative
Hemoglobin 10.9 g/dL
ESR >130 mm/hr
CRP 113 mg/L
induced sputum was trace positive for MTB on GeneXpert
biopsy of the toe ulcer showed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus
Chest radiograph showed bilateral reticular-nodular opacities
MRI of the spine revealed contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis and an epidural/paraspinal collection causing spinal cord compression

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results, including the induced sputum positive for MTB, biopsy of the toe ulcer showing necrotizing granulomatous inflammation, and MRI of the spine revealing contiguous spondylitis, are consistent with miliary tuberculosis.
The patient's chronic lower back pain and MRI of the spine revealing contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis and an epidural/paraspinal collection are consistent with Pott's disease.
The patient's painful nonhealing ulcer on his right hallux and biopsy showing necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus are consistent with tuberculous osteomyelitis.
The patient's elevated ESR and CRP, and renal ultrasound demonstrating increased echogenicity, are consistent with renal tuberculosis.
The patient's chronic lower back pain and MRI of the spine revealing contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis are consistent with tuberculous spondylodiscitis.

rationales.F01: The patient's 2-year history of progressively worsening fever is consistent with a chronic infection such as tuberculosis.
rationales.F03: Chronic lower back pain without neurologic deficits could be indicative of Pott's disease or tuberculous spondylodiscitis.
rationales.F07: Elevated ESR is a nonspecific marker of inflammation, which could be seen in various forms of tuberculosis.
rationales.F09: The induced sputum being trace positive for MTB on GeneXpert is a strong indicator of tuberculosis.
rationales.F10: The biopsy of the toe ulcer showing necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus is highly suggestive of tuberculous osteomyelitis.
rationales.F12: The MRI findings of contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis and an epidural/paraspinal collection causing spinal cord compression are consistent with tuberculous spondylodiscitis.
